newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto's son submits bank guarantee for Timor car.
newsitem.headline: Suharto's son submits bank guarantee for Timor car.

text.p: A company controlled by the youngest son of Indonesian President Suharto has submitted a bank guarantee to partly cover import duties for a controversial national car, Bisnis Indonesia daily reported on Tuesday.
The daily quoted Finance Ministry officials as saying PT Timor Putra Nasional had given bank guarantees for 2,084 Timor sedans, which were imported last month from South Korea's Kia Motors
"Now they are allowed to distribute the imported car to its dealers," one official told the newspaper.
He also said the bank guarantee comprised 25 percent of import duties but he did not say whether the company also gave a bank guarantee for luxury taxes.

Timor Putra, the only beneficiary of a national car policy announced in February, has been given a waiver on import duties and luxury taxes subject to meeting local content requirements of 20 percent in its first year of operation and 60 percent within three years.
The government has also allowed the company to import some 4,000 vehicles before it begins assembly in a local plant early next year in a joint venture with Kia Motors.
The guarantees will be exercised if the company, controlled by Suharto's son Hutomo Mandala Putra, fails to meet the local content requirements.

The national car policy has come in for severe criticism from Japan and the United States, which have said it discriminates against existing joint ventures in Indonesia, most of which are with Japanese or U.S. manufacturers.
The tax breaks will enable the Timor to be sold at about half the sticker price of comparable sedans available in Indonesia.
Japan had threatened to complain to the World Trade Organisation once the first batch of imported cars landed in Indonesia but has so far held off on the move.
